\section{Author-fixed scientific scope}
BayesBreak is the method developed in Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Segmentation with Irregular Designs, Multi-Sequence Hierarchies, and Grouped/Latent-Group Designs. For supported observation models, family-specific segment marginal likelihoods and posterior moments enter common sum-product recursions for posterior quantities and a separate max-sum recursion with backtracking for the joint MAP partition. The implementation must preserve irregular-design priors, common and group-specific changepoints across multiple sequences, known groups, and the finite latent-group criterion stated in the manuscript.

\subsection{Do not change}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt]
\item Do not change the manuscript title or replace generalized hierarchical Bayesian segmentation as the main scientific narrative without explicit author approval.
\item Do not overwrite populated archived numerical results; a corrected computation receives a new result ID and an explicit parent-result link.
\item Do not interpret the finite latent-group criterion as a normalized finite-mixture likelihood.
\item Do not use marginal changepoint modes as the joint MAP partition.
\item Do not treat agreement with BayesBreak MAP changepoints as accuracy against independent truth.
\item Do not use RES-BB-CMP-002 or RES-BB-RD-007Q in comparator or posterior-predictive conclusions.
\item Do not describe the method with vague branding; use the defined probability model, prior, recursion, optimization objective, metric, or numerical criterion.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Non-goals}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt]
\item No normalized latent-mixture model is implemented in this work program.
\item No online changepoint detector, slope-change model, or graph segmentation method is introduced.
\item No archived result is silently corrected in place.
\item No fixed package version, compute budget, or completion date is invented before version and resource profiling are resolved.
\item No slide deck is generated by this manuscript workflow.
\end{itemize}

\section{Experiment matrix and output ownership}
Each experiment driver owns a machine-readable run registry, configuration set, raw metric records, and figure or table target. Populated archived values remain read-only. Corrected runs receive a new result ID and a parent pointer.

\subsection{EPR-BB-001 -- Randomized exact-DP and semiring invariants}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-001;CLM-BB-003;CLM-BB-004\par
\textbf{Status.} executed plus expansion planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Sum-product and max-sum implementations match exhaustive enumeration on all sampled admissible finite cases.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Agreement is limited to hand-picked priors or benign support.\par
\textbf{Design.} Property-based generation over n, k\_max, local scores, zero-support blocks, priors, and ties; compare evidence, P(k), marginals, and joint MAP.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} absolute/relative error, normalization error, exact partition equality, failure count with seed.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} At least 1,000 deterministic seeded cases per configuration family; report zero-failure upper bound.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-002;CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} tests and a machine-readable invariant report.

\subsection{EPR-BB-002 -- Conjugate-family recovery and null/misspecification grid}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-002;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} executed real values plus expanded protocol planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} The common interface preserves calibrated segmentation behavior across supported families when their data model is correct.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Apparent portability is driven by a narrow SNR or tuned prior.\par
\textbf{Design.} Factorial grid over family, n, segment count, spacing, SNR, weight/exposure patterns, null data, and selected misspecification.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} boundary precision/recall/F1 under external truth, k error, posterior coverage, log evidence, runtime.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Predeclared repetitions with bootstrap or t-intervals by cell and family-level multiplicity control for headline contrasts.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-001;CODE-BB-002;CODE-BB-010\par
\textbf{Output.} family performance table, calibration plots, and null-control table.

\subsection{EPR-BB-003 -- Boundary posterior calibration}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-003;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} executed ECE/Brier values retained; expanded uncertainty and calibration checks planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Bayes curve probabilities are calibrated for the declared model after marginalizing over k.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Low aggregate ECE is caused by severe class imbalance or bin choices.\par
\textbf{Design.} Repeated simulated datasets with fixed-k and k-marginalized posterior variants; preregistered equal-width and equal-mass bins.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} Brier, log score, ECE, reliability slope/intercept, prevalence, calibration curves.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Dataset-level intervals and paired comparison of fixed-k versus marginalized variants.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-002;CODE-BB-010\par
\textbf{Output.} calibration figure with intervals and protocol sidecar.

\subsection{EPR-BB-004 -- Segment-count and SNR behavior}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-003;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} executed plus interpretation expansion planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Posterior uncertainty over k changes predictably with signal strength and prior concentration.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Observed k behavior is a prior artifact or oversegmentation bias.\par
\textbf{Design.} Cross SNR, n, true k, minimum segment length, and prior settings; include no-change and dense-change controls.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} P(k\_true), posterior entropy, k bias, boundary loss, false discoveries.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Repeated-seed intervals and decomposition by prior regime.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-001;CODE-BB-002\par
\textbf{Output.} k-posterior panels and falsification table.

\subsection{EPR-BB-005 -- Finite latent-group criterion stress test}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-008;CLM-BB-009;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} corrected stress rerun executed as RES-BB-SYN-005; archived 96 percent parent retained\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Coordinate updates monotonically improve the stated score and recover shared templates in identifiable finite simulations.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Recovery is restart luck, label coding, or collapse under overspecified G.\par
\textbf{Design.} Vary S, G\_true/G\_fit, n, noise, template separation, imbalance, initialization, and collapsed/duplicate templates.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} objective monotonicity, final objective, label-invariant ARI, template distance, collapse rate, restart selection stability.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} At least 50 datasets per cell and multiple restarts; paired pre/post repair diagnostic.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-003;CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} stress-test table, objective traces, and regression report.

\subsection{EPR-BB-006 -- Shared-boundary weak-signal pooling}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-006;CLM-BB-007\par
\textbf{Status.} executed supplementary outputs plus fair comparison planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Exact shared-boundary pooling improves boundary recovery when multiple subjects share changes and individual signals are weak.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Gains are caused by forced-sharing bias or tuned k.\par
\textbf{Design.} Vary subject count, information heterogeneity, shared fraction, subject-specific deviations, noise, and prior; compare shared, independent, and suitable multisequence methods.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} external-truth boundary loss, k error, calibration, predictive score under a common joint target, runtime.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Repeated datasets with paired contrasts and heterogeneity-stratified intervals.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-004;CODE-BB-009;CODE-BB-010\par
\textbf{Output.} pooling benefit/failure surface and model-assumption table.

\subsection{EPR-BB-007 -- Nonconjugate local certificate and global sensitivity}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-010;CLM-BB-011\par
\textbf{Status.} real benchmark values retained; certification expansion planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Measured reachable-block log-score tolerances predict the observed perturbation of evidence and posterior summaries.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Average block error hides rare reachable blocks that dominate the posterior.\par
\textbf{Design.} Construct high-accuracy references, census or sample all reachable blocks, separate truncation from numerical error, and rerun DP at nested tolerances.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} max/quantile block error, evidence ratio, posterior-odds distortion, TV distance, boundary/k changes, time/memory.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Multiple datasets and tolerance ladders; deterministic reference checks where possible.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-005;CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} certificate files and segment-to-partition error-bound table.

\subsection{EPR-BB-008 -- Runtime and memory decomposition}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-003;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} real local slopes retained; extended scaling planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Measured cost decomposes into block construction and O(k\_max n\textasciicircum{}2) DP transitions with predictable memory scaling.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Near-linear local slopes reflect cache/warmup or a narrow n range, not algorithmic structure.\par
\textbf{Design.} Extend n and k\_max until resource limits; separate cold/warm cache, block construction, DP, backtracking, and I/O; use fixed hardware and repeated runs.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} wall time, CPU time, peak RSS, transition count, slope by range, residuals against n\textasciicircum{}2 k model.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Median and dispersion across repetitions, machines reported separately.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} scaling curves, resource table, and profiler artifacts.

\subsection{EPR-BB-009 -- Well-log prior sensitivity case study}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-005;CLM-BB-014\par
\textbf{Status.} two executed real fits retained\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Cohesion and boundary-hazard choices change segmentation in interpretable ways without being mislabeled as external accuracy.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Differences are arbitrary prior sensitivity with no physical interpretation.\par
\textbf{Design.} Reproduce archived index-uniform and length-aware fits, then vary repaired c/h choices on the same 507-point stride-8 series.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} k\_hat, log evidence within a common model family, boundary stability, posterior uncertainty, runtime.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Sensitivity grid rather than sampling uncertainty; external annotations only if independently verified.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-001;CODE-BB-011;CODE-BB-015\par
\textbf{Output.} case-study figure, prior sensitivity table, provenance card.

\subsection{EPR-BB-010 -- Array-CGH shared-boundary case study}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-006;CLM-BB-014\par
\textbf{Status.} 43 by 2215 fits retained; corrected raw-matrix comparator executed as RES-BB-CMP-003; invalid parent excluded\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} The shared model provides a coherent common-boundary summary across the multisequence matrix.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Forced sharing obscures subject-specific changes or comparator conclusions arise from axis mismatch.\par
\textbf{Design.} Reproduce shared and independent fits; validate axis before every comparator; use raw matrix for multisequence baselines and common joint targets for model comparison.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} boundary summaries, subject fit diagnostics, predictive/common-target scores, external annotations when verified, runtime.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Subject bootstrap or simulation-based uncertainty where scientifically justified; no pseudo-replication across probes.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-004;CODE-BB-009;CODE-BB-011;CODE-BB-015\par
\textbf{Output.} valid multiple-sequence comparison table and provenance link to the excluded computation.

\subsection{EPR-BB-011 -- SPX regime case study}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-014\par
\textbf{Status.} Gaussian and Bernoulli fits are executed real results\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} The two declared observation models expose different posterior regime summaries over 2015-2023.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Event alignment is post hoc and family evidence values are incommensurate.\par
\textbf{Design.} Reproduce stride-4 n=566 fits, define response transformations, and predeclare any out-of-sample or contextual-event analysis.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} k\_hat, within-model evidence, posterior uncertainty, predictive score under declared target, qualitative event overlay.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Block-aware time split or rolling evaluation for predictive claims; event overlay remains descriptive.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-007;CODE-BB-011;CODE-BB-015\par
\textbf{Output.} synchronized case-study figure/caption/data card.

\subsection{EPR-BB-012 -- MethylKit chr21 segmentation and predictive repair}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-002;CLM-BB-012;CLM-BB-014\par
\textbf{Status.} segmentation retained; corrected in-support Beta predictive rerun executed as RES-BB-RD-008Q; invalid parent excluded\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} A family-correct Beta-observation predictive distribution yields a valid held-out score on a scientifically justified in-support split.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} The apparent score was an artifact of Gaussian fallback and endpoint clipping.\par
\textbf{Design.} Use exact executed methylKit test1.myCpG chr21 source, hash weights/split, implement Beta predictive, keep test coordinates in declared support or use named extrapolation, repeat block-aware splits.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} total and mean log predictive score with denominator m, calibration where defined, k\_hat, boundary stability, runtime.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Repeated splits with intervals; second region/cell type remains planned until sourced.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-006;CODE-BB-007;CODE-BB-010;CODE-BB-011\par
\textbf{Output.} new sidecar with lineage to the excluded value and corrected figure/table.

\subsection{EPR-BB-013 -- Comparator agreement, tuning fairness, and external accuracy}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-014\par
\textbf{Status.} matched-k CGH agreement executed as RES-BB-CMP-003; non-CGH agreement retained; predictive and external-truth strata planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Conclusions remain stable when matched-k agreement, independently tuned prediction, and external-truth accuracy are reported as separate tasks.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Reported superiority is induced by BayesBreak-referenced labels or asymmetric tuning.\par
\textbf{Design.} Three strata: matched-k diagnostic, equal-budget prediction tuning, and external annotation/simulation truth; canonical one-to-one matcher.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} agreement F1/Jaccard/matched MAE, predictive proper score, external precision/recall/F1, runtime and tuning cost.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Repeated splits/datasets and paired intervals; NA when no matched boundaries.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-008;CODE-BB-009;CODE-BB-010\par
\textbf{Output.} task-separated comparator table and tuning ledger.

\subsection{EPR-BB-014 -- Family-specific posterior-prediction tests}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-012\par
\textbf{Status.} MAP predictive certification executed across concrete families with unsupported logistic-normal failure explicit; model-averaged prediction remains planned\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} Every family produces finite, normalized or correctly generalized predictive scores on supported inputs and rejects unsupported extrapolation by default.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Base-class fallbacks hide family-specific errors.\par
\textbf{Design.} Unit and integration cases for each family, MAP versus model-averaged prediction, left/right out-of-range coordinates, zero weights, edge parameters, and invalid inputs.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} analytic/reference agreement, finite checks, normalization where applicable, expected exceptions, reproducibility.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Deterministic tests plus randomized property cases.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-006;CODE-BB-007;CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} prediction certification report.

\subsection{EPR-BB-015 -- Misspecification, failure-boundary, and negative-control suite}
\textbf{Claims.} CLM-BB-005;CLM-BB-007;CLM-BB-010;CLM-BB-011;CLM-BB-013\par
\textbf{Status.} final corrected bounded pilot certified; corrected 400-run full suite explicitly approved and pending execution\par
\textbf{Hypothesis.} BayesBreak fails in predictable, detectable ways under declared boundary cases.\par
\textbf{Competing explanation.} Diagnostics remain optimistic under heavy tails, zero inflation, dense changes, unequal information, or adversarial priors.\par
\textbf{Design.} Heavy tails, zero inflation, no change, dense change, short segments, unequal subject information, grid refinement, approximation failure, and prior conflict.\par
\textbf{Metrics.} false discoveries, missed changes, posterior entropy/calibration, certificate failure, runtime, warning/error behavior.\par
\textbf{Repetition and uncertainty.} Predeclared repetitions and regime-wise intervals; report reversed and null outcomes.\par
\textbf{Dependencies.} CODE-BB-001;CODE-BB-005;CODE-BB-010;CODE-BB-012\par
\textbf{Output.} failure map and decision thresholds.

\section{Logging, provenance, and resources}
\subsection{Required run records}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt]
\item Record result\_id and parent\_result\_id before writing a corrected result.
\item Record data, configuration, code, and environment hashes for every new run.
\item Store the coordinate axis, observation family, prior, split, extrapolation policy, metric version, and tuning budget with each relevant result.
\item Report executed, valid for the stated interpretation, excluded from a named analysis, and planned as separate fields.
\item Reject absolute author-local paths in release records.
\end{itemize}
\subsection{Resource planning}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt]
\item Profile the one test unresolved under the Phase 6 per-test cap before setting time or memory budgets.
\item Account explicitly for the O(n\textasciicircum{}2) segment-score table and O(k\_max n\textasciicircum{}2) worst-case partition recursions.
\item Measure sequence count, candidate count, observation family, nonconjugate method, repetitions, and comparator tuning as separate resource drivers.
\item Produce pilot-based CPU, memory, storage, and wall-time estimates before the expanded experiment grid; the current archive does not support a defensible fixed estimate.
\end{itemize}

\section{Explicit failure states}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-001]
\textbf{Condition.} Nonfinite or dimensionally inconsistent segment scores.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Stop before partition inference and emit the offending family, segment coordinates, and configuration hash.
\end{cautionbox}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-002]
\textbf{Condition.} Comparator prediction and reference axes differ.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Reject metric computation; preserve the attempted run only as a diagnostic record.
\end{cautionbox}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-003]
\textbf{Condition.} Posterior prediction requested for an unsupported family or coordinate outside support.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Raise an explicit error unless a named, recorded extrapolation rule is selected.
\end{cautionbox}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-004]
\textbf{Condition.} Latent-group objective is nonmonotone beyond tolerance or returned objective differs from the final trace value.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Mark the restart invalid and do not select it as the optimum.
\end{cautionbox}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-005]
\textbf{Condition.} A required test exceeds its profiled bound.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Report unresolved with owner, environment, seed, and profile; do not count it as a pass.
\end{cautionbox}
\begin{cautionbox}[FAIL-BB-006]
\textbf{Condition.} A corrected result lacks a parent link or required hashes.\par
\textbf{Required behavior.} Reject release of the result and retain the archived parent unchanged.
\end{cautionbox}

\section{Definition of done}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=1.5pt,topsep=2pt]
\item The exact title and generalized hierarchical Bayesian segmentation narrative remain unchanged across the book, main paper, executive summary, code handoff, and presentation handoffs.
\item Exact finite-case dynamic-programming properties match exhaustive enumeration under seeded tests.
\item Posterior prediction is family-specific and out-of-range coordinates follow an explicit recorded policy.
\item Comparator axes, reference type, matching rule, and tuning budget are validated before metric computation.
\item Every corrected result has a new ID, a parent link, and data, configuration, code, and environment hashes; archived populated values remain unchanged.
\item Book appendix, standalone coding handoff, repository registries, figures, tables, and metadata pass synchronization checks.
\item Every unresolved proof, test, computation, annotation, or release decision is stated directly rather than represented as complete.
\end{itemize}
